title: External inventory allocation reserve line
description: One hold placed on exactly one warehouse lot. Field names and vocabulary match external-inventory-allocation.schema.json so the same reader can consume both the reserve result and the allocation snapshot.

item_id.description: Provider-side inventory item identity for the held lot. It is not the SKU identifier; resolve stock by SKU through the reserve request or the allocation snapshot filters.

status.description: A freshly created hold is always RESERVED. CONFIRMED and ISSUED are reached only by warehouse operations; the sales platform cannot drive those transitions. RELEASED is reached by warehouse release, by hold expiry, or by the consumer itself through POST /v1/inventory/allocations/release. Lines of an ALREADY_RESERVED answer repeat the state of the existing hold, so they can be CONFIRMED; ISSUED is accepted by this schema only so that every allocation projection shares one status vocabulary; it is not emitted on this route, because a source whose allocation of the same principal was already issued is answered 409 ALLOCATION_CONFLICT (and an issued allocation of another principal, 409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK). See enums/ops/inventory-allocation-status.yaml.

requested_at.description: When the provider received the call that created this hold (provider time; not a request field). A repeat call or an extension never changes it, and the maximum total hold (48 hours by default, QT-CHUNG-016) counts from it. A hold placed after a release has a new requested_at.

expires_at.description: When the hold of this line expires. On a 200 ALREADY_RESERVED answer it is the current expiry, after any extension made by that call; a replay of the original idempotency key returns the original value. An extension never moves it past requested_at plus the provider's maximum total hold (48 hours by default, QT-CHUNG-016): a later value is cut to that moment, so it can be earlier than the expires_at the call sent.
